properties.headline: Flood Warning issued October 14 at 9:36AM EDT by NWS Melbourne FL
properties.description:
...Forecast flooding changed from Minor to Moderate severity for the
following rivers in Florida...

St Johns River Near Astor affecting Lake and Volusia Counties.

.The St Johns River at Astor is forecast to remain in Minor Flood
Stage through Friday, as previous heavy rainfall continues to drain
through the basin. However, strong northeasterly winds this weekend
are forecast to lead a return to Moderate Flood Stage.

For the St. Johns River...including Astor...Moderate flooding is
forecast.

* WHAT...Minor flooding is occurring and moderate flooding is
forecast.

* WHERE...St Johns River near Astor.

* WHEN...Until further notice.

* IMPACTS...At 2.8 feet, Docks and boat ramps covered at South Moon
Fish Camp and approaching sea wall at Blair's Jungle Den. Water
approaching sites closest to the river at Fish Tales RV Resort and
Astor Landing Campground. Portion of Clair Street covered by river
water south of the Butler Boat Ramp. Docks underwater at the Astor
Bridge Marina and along Riveredge Drive. Portions of Fox Road are
covered with water nearest to the river. Acorn, Hazelnut and Redbud
roads are underwater with yards inundated. At 3.0 feet, Water
approaches or may enter lowest homes on or near Wildhog Road and
nearby canals. Flooding reaches the parking lot of the Juno Trail
Apartments. Flooding on portions of Alligator Road and Holiday
Road. Lowest lying yards along Blue Creek are flooded. Roads at
Astor Landing Campground and Lake Dexter Boat Ramp begin to flood.
Water enters lower homes closest to the river on McPherson Lane.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 8:30 AM EDT Wednesday the stage was 2.8 feet.
- Bankfull stage is 2.0 feet.
- Recent Activity...The maximum river stage in the 24 hours ending
at 8:30 AM EDT Wednesday was 2.9 feet.
- Forecast...The river is expected to remain steady above flood
stage at 2.8 feet.
- Flood stage is 2.3 feet.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood

properties.description:
FFWLUB

The National Weather Service in Lubbock has extended the

* Flash Flood Warning for...
Southeastern Crosby County in northwestern Texas...
Southwestern Dickens County in northwestern Texas...
Northeastern Garza County in northwestern Texas...
Northwestern Kent County in northwestern Texas...

* Until 845 PM CDT.

* At 658 PM CDT, Doppler radar indicated that the heaviest rain has
ended across the warned area, but light rain will continue over the
next hour or so which will result in the continuation of flash
flooding. Between 2 and 5 inches of rain have fallen. Flash
flooding is already occurring.

HAZARD...Flash flooding caused by thunderstorms.

SOURCE...Radar indicated.

IMPACT...Flash flooding of small creeks and streams, urban areas,
highways, streets and underpasses as well as other poor
drainage and low-lying areas.

* Some locations that will experience flash flooding include...
White River Lake and Kalgary.

deaths occur in vehicles.

properties.headline: Severe Thunderstorm Warning issued October 14 at 7:48PM CDT until October 14 at 8:30PM CDT by NWS Midland/Odessa TX
properties.description:
At 748 PM CDT, a severe thunderstorm was located 21 miles southwest
of Sanderson, moving north at 30 mph.

HAZARD...Ping pong ball size hail and 60 mph wind gusts.

SOURCE...Radar indicated.

IMPACT...People and animals outdoors will be injured. Expect hail
damage to roofs, siding, windows, and vehicles. Expect wind
damage to roofs, siding, and trees.

This severe thunderstorm will remain over mainly rural areas of south
central Pecos, east central Brewster and west central Terrell
Counties.
properties.instruction:
For your protection move to an interior room on the lowest floor of a
building.

Torrential rainfall is occurring with this storm, and may lead to
flash flooding. Do not drive your vehicle through flooded roadways.
